text:
sam: Hey all — first day, trying to finish k8s setup from the onboarding doc. I copied the kubeconfig to ~/.kube/config but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows nothing. Any obvious step I missed?
elaine: welcome @sam! :wave: Did you run the onboarding helper? https://internal.redwood.dev/onboarding/k8s — it runs the SSO flow and writes a context for you.
sam: I ran it but when I try `kubectl get ns` I get `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`.
jun: That usually means `kubectl` is old or your exec plugin didn't run. What does `kubectl version --client --short` show?
sam: `Client Version: v1.21.0`
jun: Ah — our auth exec requires >= v1.23. Upgrade (brew/asdf) then re-run `redwood-devex auth sso --kube`.
sam: upgraded to v1.25 and re-ran. Now `kubectl config get-contexts` shows `dev/sam@redwood-dev`. I tried `kubectl use-context dev/sam@redwood-dev` and `kubectl get ns` but it's `Forbidden`.
elaine: New hires get a sandbox namespace by default named `sandbox-<username>`. I can provision one for you if Jun hasn't yet.
sam: I tried `kubectl get ns sandbox-sam` and it said not found.
jun: I just queued provisioning. k8s-bot should post status.
k8s-bot: Provision request queued (req-789). ETA ~2m.
jun: Done — `sandbox-sam` created and a RoleBinding to `edit` should be in place. Try `kubectl get ns sandbox-sam` again.
sam: Namespace exists now but `kubectl -n sandbox-sam get pods` returns `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "sam@redwood" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "sandbox-sam"`.
jun: Hmm, your IDP groups didn't map. New hires are put into `group:developers` for RBAC. Can you run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n sandbox-sam` and paste output?
sam: It prints `no`.
jun: Okay I'm checking the mapping — IDP sends the group claim under `memberOf` but our OIDC mapping expects `groups`. I'll patch the claim mapping and rebind.
elaine: Quick checklist for future folks: 1) upgrade kubectl to >= v1.23, 2) run `redwood-devex auth sso --kube` (opens SSO), 3) check `kubectl config get-contexts`, 4) wait for namespace provisioning, 5) if you see "forbidden" check group sync and run `kubectl auth can-i`.
sam: After Jun's patch and clearing cache (`rm -rf ~/.kube/cache`), re-login, `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n sandbox-sam` now returns `yes`. ✅
sam: One more question — who's the point person for prod kube access requests?
elaine: For prod: open the "prod-access" request form on Confluence and ping #eng-security, cc Jun and ops-oncall. We need the ticket for audit.
sam: Thanks everyone — this helped a lot. Closing thread. :tada:
